aula.objetivo: Form the pretérito imperfecto of -ar, -er and -ir verbs and the three irregulars (ser, ir, ver), and use it for past habits, descriptions, age, time, and weather, while avoiding three false friends: «exquisito», «embarazada», and «raro».

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: the pretérito imperfecto describes the past without saying when it started or when it ended. It's for what used to be habitual, for descriptions, and for the backdrop of a scene. «De niño vivía en Sevilla» (I lived there as a child — no telling how long). STEP 2: for -ar verbs, drop the «-ar» and add: -aba, -abas, -aba, -ábamos, -abais, -aban. «Hablar» becomes «hablaba, hablabas, hablaba, hablábamos, hablabais, hablaban». STEP 3: for -er and -ir verbs, drop the ending and add: -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían. «Comer» becomes «comía, comías, comía, comíamos, comíais, comían». «Vivir» becomes «vivía, vivías, vivía, vivíamos, vivíais, vivían». STEP 4: «yo» and «él, ella, usted» share the same form: «hablaba», «comía». When that's ambiguous, add the pronoun: «Yo vivía en Lima y ella vivía en Cusco». STEP 5: the written accent is required on «-ía» (always) and on «-ábamos» (nosotros, -ar). Without it, the pronunciation is wrong — there's no such word as «comia» in Spanish. STEP 6: -ar verbs are spelled with a «b» in «-aba». STEP 7: this tense is regular even for verbs that change their stem in the present: «dormir» becomes «dormía» (not «durmía»), «tener» becomes «tenía», «hacer» becomes «hacía». STEP 8: the typical markers are «de niño», «antes», «siempre», «cada día», «todos los veranos», «a menudo», «normalmente», «entonces», and «mientras».
blocos.comparacao: English has no dedicated conjugation for this tense at all — it leans on «used to» + infinitive («I used to live there») or just the plain simple past, with context doing all the work of signaling habit versus a one-off event. Spanish, by contrast, marks the distinction directly in the verb's own ending, so «hablaba» can never be mistaken for a single finished action the way English «I talked» can mean either a habit or a one-time event depending on what surrounds it. Because English gives you no verb-shape cue to lean on here, the endings themselves — and especially the written accent on «-ía» and «-ábamos» — are the part worth drilling hardest.

exemplos.pt: As a child I used to work at a bank.

exemplos.ru: De pequeña vivíamos cerca del mar.
exemplos.pt: When I was little, we used to live near the sea.
My grandparents used to have a vegetable garden.

erros.motivo: The written accent on «-ía» is required.
The «nosotros» form carries an accent on «-ábamos».
In the imperfecto, verbs that change their vowel in the present don't change it here.
The plural of -er and -ir verbs is «-ían», with an accent.

blocos.enunciado: Say five sentences about what your life was like as a child: where you lived, where you went to school, what you used to eat, who you used to play with. Use «De niño…» or «De niña…».
Say five sentences in the indefinido about last weekend, using at least two irregular verbs (fui, vi, hice, tuve, dije…).
